overall: The Granby Finance Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific 'FY-25 Budget' notice for its May 23 meeting; other allegations were not violations or were declined, and no further remedy was ordered because the video is public and the warrant articles passed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the May 23 notice topic 'FY-25 Budget' was too vague to tell the public the Committee would discuss the Fire Department.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific notice for its May 23 meeting where the notice did not reasonably advise the public that the Committee would discuss the Fire Department and Ambulance Department budgets, the Fire Chief’s management of these budgets, and the Special Town Meeting warrant proposing to transfer funds to the two departments.

allegations.summary: The AG noted, though no one alleged it, that the eleven earlier notices used the same or nearly the same generic topics and were likely insufficient too.
allegations.key_passage: We do not make a formal finding regarding the sufficiency of these notices but note that they too were likely insufficient for the same reasons as explained above.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee discussed a specific individual at the May 23 meeting without first giving that person notice that they would be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: we find no violation where the May 23 meeting was held in open session and the Open Meeting Law does not require direct notice be given to an individual unless that individual will be discussed in executive session under G.L. c. 30A, § 21(a)(1)

allegations.summary: Complainant argued on further review that some May 23 topics fell outside the Committee's jurisdiction.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, an allegation that a public body discussed matters outside of its jurisdiction, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the meeting was slanderous and that the Committee's actions could subject the Town to litigation.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, allegations of slander or that the Committee’s actions could subject the Town to litigation fall outside of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (ordered). The AG cautioned that similar future violations could be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
